Swiss Army Bench 0.0.13: Trino keystore sign-in, the Session page, and longer time limits.

- **Trino with a client certificate:** Sign in offers "Client certificate (keystore)". The keystore is read by its
  contents (PKCS#12, or the older Java format with the small pyjks package, offered when needed); its password is a
  secret like any other. Test now runs a real query, so "signed in" means Trino let you in.
- **Certificate and keystore files from an environment variable:** any connection's certificate or keystore file
  can be a plain path or come from a variable (such as TRINO_KEYSTORE_PATH) with this computer's path as the
  default, so the same code runs here and in a function app. Export as one script lists the variable to set.
- **Session page** (on the rail): what the agent made or changed this session, each with a link to it. **Follow
  the agent** (on by default) brings up where it is working and highlights what changed, live, without ever
  interrupting your typing.
- **"Install <package>?"** appears right away when something needs a package that is not installed: Install now,
  or Not now (a small reminder stays).
- **Save, Save as…, Close and Autosave** sit in the Application row, with the project's name.
- **Load all rows** on a database connection: every table from it opens whole.
- **10-minute time limits** for connections, queries and the Key Finder (they were 30 seconds to 5 minutes); a
  Trino connection asks its client for 10 minutes too. A Trino connection saved before this release gets it once
  you open it and Save.

Update from the tray (right-click, Update to 0.0.13), or:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/DylanCodyBrown/SwissArmyBench/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
```
